posts.html:
Most of what I point a camera at ends up being sky. A ridge holding the last light, monsoon clouds stacking over a valley, or a road that disappears exactly where the horizon begins.

This is a running collection of those frames — the ones that survived the camera roll. The set below is a sketchbook stand-in while the full-resolution archive gets sorted; the captions are the notes I kept.

meta.title: Sub-Millisecond Canvas: Taming 60fps Data Streams Without Dropping Frames
meta.summary: Architecting zero-allocation render loops, Web Workers, and OffscreenCanvas pipelines for industrial-grade creative dev.

posts.html:
The modern web runtime is extraordinarily fast until you ask the Garbage Collector to clean up 50,000 transient JavaScript objects every frame.

When building the Downlink telemetry system, standard React state hooks proved fatal to sustained 60 FPS execution. Every re-render triggered micro-stutters during high-speed sensor bursts.

The solution was architectural decoupling: React manages the shell and navigation state, while raw telemetry streams directly into a SharedArrayBuffer managed by an OffscreenCanvas worker.

Treat the browser like a low-latency instrument. Pre-allocate your buffers, respect memory layout, and let the GPU do what it was built for.

meta.title: Why Every Designer Needs an Audio Identity & Tactile Micro-Interactions
meta.summary: Exploring synthesized Web Audio, tactile haptics, and why the physical bulb horn remains the world's most communicative sound.

posts.html:
The human ear processes auditory signals in under 10 milliseconds — more than twice as fast as visual stimuli.

Yet for two decades, web interfaces have been completely deaf and mute. We click sterile plastic screens without tactile or acoustic feedback.

Integrating the Web Audio API does not mean playing obnoxious MP3 sound effects. It means synthesizing micro-acoustic harmonics that confirm user actions with pleasant, warm resonance.

When a user taps "Horn OK Please" on this site, we synthesize dual harmonic frequencies with a gentle band-pass filter and compressor, evoking the iconic brass horn with zero external audio assets.
